Return the next passage of fiction.

item.text:
You leave the provisional curriculum on the table and listen.

Ashara speaks next. “Who chooses which completed cases the delegations submit?”

“Each delegation nominates a file,” Windwhisper says. “Faculty may accept it, reject it, or request a different one.”

“Then every office decides what it is willing to let us see.”

Kira answers from beside the blackboard. “Yes. That is why you are not graded on accepting the packet’s account of itself. Missing testimony, unexplained costs, convenient dates, and remedies no one could enforce all belong in your analysis.”

Ashara makes a brief note in her folder. Rashid does the same.

Windwhisper moves on to the rules governing simulations and observation. Conclave students may not invoke family authority during Academy exercises. They must identify themselves as students when corresponding with working delegations. Gifts, private briefings, and promises of future office must be disclosed to faculty.

Thessaly lifts one hand.

“Anything we sign during a simulation is legally void outside it.”

“All exercise documents are marked and countersigned as nonoperative,” Windwhisper confirms. “No simulation will create a debt, bargain, oath, or continuing obligation.”

Thessaly lowers her hand and returns to the printed rules.

The orientation proceeds through committee etiquette, travel permissions, and the process for requesting access to closed proceedings. No one directs another question at you. Windwhisper answers practical concerns precisely; Kira supplies examples drawn from failed negotiations and badly prepared petitions.

After forty minutes, Windwhisper closes her folder.

“Ten minutes. When you return, Professor Shaan will assign the opening exercise.”

Chairs shift around the oval table. Ashara rises to stretch the shoulder she trained that morning, while Rashid remains seated to finish copying a date from the board. The first portion of orientation ends without requiring anything further from you.
